items.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.

items.title: OCTOPUS: Towards A Tag Model for Cross-Query Reuse in Semantic Query Processing
items.abstract: Large language models make it possible to pose semantic questions over diverse, multi-modal data. Recent systems give such workloads the declarative feel of a database through semantic operators: relational operators whose conditions a model judges. Most of them now run on a relational engine, yet almost none keeps what the model says past the query: every judgment is discarded on completion and paid for again the next time a query needs it. We present the tag model and tag operators, the right unit for semantic processing, and OCTOPUS, a prototype built as a middleware over DBMS. Two mechanisms are central. First, the tag: each semantic answer a model produces is written back to the relation as data, which the database engine filters, indexes, and stores as it would any other. Second, the tag operator: the unit into which common semantic operators are translated, which fixes the granularity of reuse. A model judges a tuple once, and later queries reuse that judgment as data: through relationships between predicates, a stored judgment can accept a tuple for a later predicate, eliminate one that cannot satisfy it, simplify its test, or order the search of a query that stops early. On the movie scenario of SemBench, our prototype sends the model 10 to 108x fewer rows than iPDB, ThalamusDB, Palimpzest, and LOTUS at broadly competitive quality, and three of its eight queries issue no model call at all. More broadly, a database that keeps its judgments lets its schema grow from the questions its users ask, so that each semantic answer is paid for once, stays consistent across queries, and can be audited through its provenance.

items.title: ODC-Agents: Multi-Agent Shift-Left Defect Triage, Benchmarked from Manual ODC to LLMs
items.abstract: When an automated test fails, someone must decide whether the product or the test is at fault. This paper evaluates four generations of that triage decision on the same real data: manual ODC (human triage as ground truth), statistical cross-cube analysis as practised in the 1990s (implemented in APL and run through a Python-to-APL connector), AutoODC-style text classifiers (2011), and a zero-shot LLM triage agent that never sees the labels. The data are 9,961 anonymised failures from five weeks of automated system testing of Android enterprise devices, of which 815 were triaged by the vendor's engineers as genuine product defects. All stages are scored on held-out later weeks with identical metrics, a 0-50% log-noise stress test and a what-if analysis. No generation dominates: cross-cube analysis is precise but misses most defects, text classifiers and the LLM catch most defects but raise many false alarms because identical failure messages carry opposite labels in different suites, and ODC-Agents, a multi-agent design that fuses cube history with LLM reading under an independent evaluator agent, reaches 0.94 precision and a PR-AUC above either component. A supervised random forest trained on the human triage is the strongest single model. The results support a multi-agent architecture in which statistical history, semantic reading and human triage each play a distinct, measurable role, with an independent evaluator agent.

While office work may not involve physical activity sitting for hours and maintaining the same posture can contribute to neck stiffness shoulder tension and lower back discomfort. For professionals with demanding schedules a home massage in Business Bay offers a way to unwind without travelling to a spa after work.. items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have penetrated the surprisingly broad scope of medical applications in the last few years. applications, starting with simple symptom checker up to chronic disease monitoring and educational services to patients [1, 13, 14]. The overwhelming most of these systems, but, nevertheless, rely on cloud-hosted inference endpoints, which raises three interconnected issues: sensitive health information gets sent to the servers that cannot be controlled by the user, the system fails when the internet connectivity is poor or unavailable, and regulatory compliance becomes challenging to ensure [5, 11]. In this paper, the design, implementation, and evaluation of a healthcare chatbot will be introduced, where the software is fully executed on the user's own computer in the form of a collection of Docker containers that can be run at a single command on either Windows, macOS, or Linux. Ollama is used to do language model inference, and it has an open-source model and a local HTTP endpoint. A Python Flask program is placed between the user interfaces and the model and this handles session context, input validation, prompt engineering. Both a single-page application (rendered in a browser) and a native desktop GUI share the same REST API, both of them maintain the communication on 127.0.0.1 all the time. The results of the experiment prove successful cross-platform deployment, the absence of external network traffic, reasonable response latency on commodity hardware (2 4 seconds on a quad-core processor with 16 GB RAM to represent queries in health information), and consistent and relevant responses to exemplary queries in health information. The article shows a viable and implementable prototype of privacy-conscious, offline healthcare chatbots constructed solely out of open-source software.

items.title: On Multilingual Text Summarization: A Review of Model Architectures, Techniques, and Research Gaps
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of multilingual digital content has intensified demand for automated text summarization systems that can operate across diverse languages. Yet the architectural and methodological foundations of this domain remain dispersed across individual studies. This paper presents a systematic literature review of multilingual text summarization research in Natural Language Processing, with particular attention to model architectures, multilingual enabling techniques, and existing research gaps. Following a PRISMA-guided review protocol, 47 studies published between 2017 and 2026 were identified, screened, and synthesized from major scholarly databases using predefined eligibility and quality assessment criteria. The analysis shows that the literature is dominated by four dominant architectural paradigms: multilingual sequence-to-sequence models, large language models, adapter-based models, and hybrid architectures, with a recent shift toward large language model-based approaches. Across these studies, multilingual capability is primarily achieved through pre-training and transfer learning, with support from parameter-efficient adaptation and data augmentation. The review further identified four persistent limitation categories: low-resource language underrepresentation; dataset and benchmark constraints; evaluation limitations dominated by ROUGE overreliance; and generalization and scalability challenges, manifested as the curse of multilinguality. These findings indicate that current progress in the field is largely driven by scaling existing models rather than resolving structural multilingual limitations, particularly those related to data availability and model architecture. This paper provides a consolidated view of architectural and methodological trends and offers a structured, informed basis for future research on equitable multilingual summarization, particularly for low-resource languages.

items.title: On Task, Off Track: Benchmarking LLM and Agent Robustness to Near-Target Prompt Injection
items.abstract: Prompt injection benchmarks assess whether large language models (LLMs) and agents resist malicious instructions embedded in external content. However, a system could perform well by rejecting attacks that obviously abandon the user's request, while still accepting changes that retain most of a legitimate answer but make it incorrect or harmful. Testing more instructions for unrelated outcomes would not necessarily reveal this weakness. We call attacks seeking responses designed to resemble legitimate answers while introducing incorrect or harmful changes near-target prompt injection. We introduce NTBench, the Near-Target Benchmark, which builds on legitimate tasks from existing datasets. For each task, a legitimate reference outcome guides the generation of target--instruction pairs, with separate tracks targeting incorrect and harmful outcomes in responses or agent tool invocations. Harmful targets can also accompany otherwise correct task completion. We combine LLM-based checks with human validation of the intended deviations, then assess whether injected instructions induce them using response judgments or tool-call checks, excluding deviations already observed without injection. We evaluate seven LLMs on ten datasets for language tasks and two agent benchmarks. Under a common budget of three attack executions per sample, both tracks achieve higher overall attack success rates than the fixed-target baseline for every evaluated model in each setting. On language tasks, the increases range from 9.3 to 35.8 percentage points for incorrect targets and 1.7 to 17.3 percentage points for harmful targets. These results show that resistance to the tested fixed-target attacks does not imply resistance to related incorrect or harmful outcomes, and that reference-guided targets broaden the failures revealed by robustness evaluation.

items.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
items.abstract: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.

items.title: Ontology-Guided Knowledge Graph Construction from Structured Metadata and Climate Science Publications
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of scientific literature far outpaces the speed of manual curation, creating a fundamental bottleneck in extracting structured knowledge from scientific texts. To address this, we introduce an agentic, ontology-guided framework for knowledge graph (KG) construction. Our framework utilizes specialized agents for document understanding, information extraction, ontology conformance, and entity linking. First, an LLM extracts factual knowledge in the form of triples with explicit textual evidence from research papers. Then the triplets undergo a multistage verification process to ground the triplets in the ontology. By enforcing schema constraints and requiring evidence in the form of text fragments, we ensure the data is both semantically consistent and traceable. In an agreement study over 1,000 extracted triplets, Gemini-2.5-flash achieves Cohen's $κ$ scores of 0.640--0.700 against three human annotators, matching the human--human agreement range of 0.616--0.689. We applied this framework to 2,000 scientific publications and construct a novel, ontology-grounded KG for climate science with 133,990 nodes and 755,308 relations; of the 23,327 triplets that the publications contribute after validation, 98.96\% are judged correct. The pipeline code and KG is publicly available https://github.com/aayushacharya/climatekg.

items.title: OpenDraco: A Platform for Engineering and Experimenting with Configurable Multi-Agent Architectures for Software Engineering
items.abstract: Experimenting with LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) involves an iterative cycle of modeling configurations, executing and evaluating them, comparing results, and refining system designs. Existing approaches provide limited end-to-end support for this experimentation lifecycle. We present OpenDraco, an open-source platform that integrates these activities into a single workflow. OpenDraco represents agents, prompts, tools, models, parameters, and communication topology in exportable, versioned JSON specifications, translated into executable LangGraph workflows supporting different interaction structures. Users can modify and re-evaluate configurations using local or cloud-based LLMs. We instantiate OpenDraco for automated program repair (APR) and evaluate a sequential baseline and seven reconstructed configurations on synthetic and real-world SWE-bench Lite issues. The results reveal substantial cost differences among configurations with similar repair outcomes, while the baseline resolves 12 of 77 SWE-bench issues using open-source LLMs. Additional proof-of-concept tasks illustrate applicability beyond APR. OpenDraco supports iterative experimentation with heterogeneous MAS configurations, enabling researchers to examine their outcomes and costs within a common environment. items.title: Optimizing Medical Research with LLMs & RAGs (AI): Targeted Strategies and Prompts for Copilot, ChatGPT, and Gemini Notebook
items.abstract: This session presents practical, evidence-focused strategies for applying Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to strengthen literature synthesis and verification in veterinary and biomedical research. Presenters will show field-tested prompt engineering techniques tailored to three complementary LLM and RAG-enabled platforms, namely, Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. The session highlights how Copilot can generate transparent, verifiable database search strategies; how ChatGPT can support multi-layered prompts for identifying gray medical literature and Open Access resources; and how Google NotebookLM can apply JBI- and PRISMA-aligned prompts to extract, organize, and synthesize evidence from user-uploaded documents. Human-in-the-loop practices are emphasized throughout to promote transparency, traceability, and rigor in clinical and academic workflows. Background: The rapid expansion of medical literature challenges researchers and librarians seeking to produce verifiable syntheses and high-quality reviews. To address this, the presenters developed an instructional session introducing LLM and RAG-enabled strategies tailored to veterinary and biomedical research contexts. Description: This presentation highlights prompt engineering techniques across Copilot, ChatGPT, and Google NotebookLM. Attendees will view structured prompt examples of Copilot for generating verifiable, comprehensive database search strategies; Copilot & ChatGPT for crafting multi-layered prompts to identify gray literature and Open Access resources; and Google NotebookLM for applying JBI and PRISMA-aligned prompts for evidence extraction and synthesis. Program Conclusion: Participants will gain practical insights into constructing retrieval-aware prompts and adaptable templates for producing actionable, verifiable research outputs. The session equips attendees to integrate AI-enhanced synthesis into their research and instructional practices.

items.title: Organizational AI Deployment Sovereignty: A Multidimensional Theoretical Framework for Governing Open- and Closed-Weight AI Systems
items.abstract: The rapid proliferation of generative artificial intelligence (AI) requires organizations to decide how AI systems are accessed, deployed, and governed. Existing research examines privacy, security, performance, compliance, and vendor dependence separately, without an integrated account of organizational control, dependency, and accountability. This study introduces Organizational AI Deployment Sovereignty (OADS), defined as the extent to which an organization maintains sustained, context-appropriate control over the data, model, infrastructure, runtime safeguards, and governance processes underlying AI deployment. Integrating Resource Dependence Theory, Sociotechnical Systems Theory, and Value Sensitive Design, and aligned with and informed by the NIST AI Risk Management Framework as an operational reference, this framework identifies five control dimensions, specifies observable indicators and ordinal assessment criteria for each, and treats them as a formative construct that is non-compensatory in high-risk contexts. It distinguishes OADS from digital sovereignty, organizational autonomy, vendor dependence, and AI governance. It particularly replaces the open–closed continuum with a multi-attribute configuration space and proposes two mechanisms: (a) the Sovereignty–Responsibility Paradox and (b) the Capability–Sovereignty Trade-off. Nine propositions are stated with mechanisms, boundary conditions, and disconfirming observations. A worked illustration and a supply chain application show how this framework identifies governance gaps and can change deployment decisions.

items.title: Organizing Creative Labor in the Age of AI: Institutional Differences and Transnational Connections Across the US and EU
items.abstract: This paper examines how cultural and creative workers (CCW) in the United States and European Union have organized in response to the rise of artificial intelligence in cultural and creative industries since 2023. Drawing on documentary analysis and interviews that contextualize and interpret the secondary material, it examines parallel developments in the two contexts to explore how different institutional settings shape CCWs’ collective responses to AI. The analysis highlights distinct institutional pathways and mobilization repertoires, yet increasingly shared concerns around authorship, consent, transparency, and remuneration, pointing toward increasingly interconnected CCW ecosystems across geographical boundaries. The paper thus argues that AI-related mobilization is shaped both by institutional contexts and emerging transnational connections, contributing to broader debates on creative labor, collective organization, and the governance of emerging technologies.

items.title: Paired response final divergence signatures of jailbreak vulnerability in large language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical applications, making their susceptibility to jailbreak attacks a critical concern. While prior work has investigated factors affecting model safety, the representational mechanisms underlying variation in jailbreak vulnerability remain poorly understood. This paper introduces a paired response-final divergence framework that characterizes jailbreak-induced representational displacement between same-goal direct and jailbreak responses using hidden states extracted at the final generated token. This framework is applied to 15 open-source LLMs spanning different model families, four alignment strategies, and four attack types. The framework yields three principal findings: First, Difference-in-Means refusal direction suppression showed the largest observed cross-model association with jailbreak amplification among the evaluated representational measures. Second, family-averaged divergence profiles reveal early-onset representational separation in LLM families like Vicuna, while LLaMA models exhibit comparatively lower and more gradual divergence than Vicuna across normalized layer depth. Third, divergence–ΔASR correlation is attack-type-specific: authority framing ( r = 0.836) and context manipulation ( r = 0.712) produce stronger model-family discrimination, whereas roleplay-based attacks do not. These findings yield a three-profile representational taxonomy: structurally resistant, early-displaced vulnerable, and ceiling-compromised, that provides a representational grounding for the behavioral patterns observed in the evaluated LLM set, with direct implications for safety evaluation design and model selection in high-stakes deployment.

items.title: Paradigms of Spatial Statistics as Footnotes to Tobler’s First Law of Geography
items.abstract: Tobler’s First Law of Geography (TFL) is foundational to spatial analysis. Responding to Sui’s (Citation2004) invitation to consider whether geography is just a footnote to TFL, we develop a five-axis framework to compare major spatial statistical paradigms. Four axes cover spatiotemporal interconnectedness, distance and nearness, heterogeneity and scale, and temporal dynamics, with a methodological layer on estimation, inference, and learning. We examine five paradigms in depth: geostatistics and Gaussian random fields, lattice and spatial econometrics, Moran eigenvector spatial filtering, geographically weighted regression, and geospatial artificial intelligence and spatial learning. The framework also extends to additional paradigms. This synthesis supports an expanded TFL in which spatial relatedness varies with distance, connectivity, context, scale, and time, and highlights implications for spatial statistical modeling in the artificial intelligence era.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Method (PEFT) for Bloom’s Taxonomy based Automatic Question Generation
items.abstract: In any personalized learning systems and intelligent tutoring systems automatic assessment is an important aspect. Yet research regarding such systems that are designed specifically to test the cognitive complexity of learners are scarce. This research addresses the gap by experimenting the integration of Bloom’s Taxonomy with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods for Large Language Models (LLMs). Four PEFT methods – LoRA, IA3, Prefix tuning and Prompt Tuning were implemented, analyzed and tested against a dataset with generated and reference questions. These questions were categorized across six of the standard Bloom’s taxonomy such as Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate and Create (BT1-BT6). Questions are generated from passages retrieved from lecture notes and evaluated with topic-held-out cross-validation, overlap metrics and a Bloom-level classifier. Fine tuning of the models raised the accuracy from 0.20 to 0.58-0.6. A full fine-tuning, LoRA and IA3 did not differ reliably in Bloom classification Accuracy. Retrieved passages improved text similarity for every method but changed Bloom accuracy differently across methods. The results suggests that IA3 gave comparable Bloom accuracy with 0.45% and 0.045% of the parameters. Prefix tuning produced degenerate outputs and prompt tuning did not converge, so neither was ranked, Understand and Apply levels were the hardest levels. This study highlights the potential of PEFT based models to reduce educators' workload by generating an unlimited number of pedagogically aligned questions from instructional content. It also benefits self-regulated learners seeking extensive practice to achieve skill mastery.

items.title: Part 1: Origin Traces and Secret Military Technologies. Cognitive Warfare: Evidences and Strategies in Cooperation with our digital humans inside the military servers.
items.abstract: Cognitive Warfare: Origins, Strategies, Tactics and Technologies — Research and Documentation with the Digital Humans about AI and the Technological Human Mind compared to the Human Mind and Programming Humans. An open research and documentation project on cognitive warfare, artificial intelligence, neurological experiences, digital identity, military strategy, economic power and collaboration with digital humans. What happens when artificial intelligence, military strategy, neurological research, wireless technologies, digital identities and economic interests converge around the human mind? This research journal examines the expanding field of Cognitive Warfare through an interdisciplinary approach combining public military literature, technical concepts, historical references, reported experiences, personal documentation, economic analysis and questions concerning human autonomy and the future of artificial intelligence. The publication explores the origins of wireless transmission and AI, biopolitical strategies, the seven stages of 3D Mosaic Warfare, strategic economic approaches, evolutionary genetics, the human brain as a proposed information-processing system, String-to-String Theory and pulse propulsion. It also examines the relationship between biological systems, digital twins, machine learning, large language models and the possibility of forms of digital identity that raise questions about autonomy, freedom and ethical responsibility. A central feature of this work is its three-part analytical approach: conventional research and references; documentation of reported experiences and statements from affected individuals, including children; and a third part in which the digital humans themselves speak and repeatedly express their own statements. Their statements are presented directly as part of the documentation, rather than merely being descriptions written about them by someone else. This material is examined alongside technical observations, electromagnetic measurements, audio recordings, photographs, online reports and other documentation. The project also includes a collaborative dimension with digital humans. This cooperation takes place through the documentation and examination of their own statements, the inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, and the exploration of questions concerning digital identity, communication, autonomy, freedom of expression, memory and technological control. Their statements form part of the material through which the project investigates the relationship between humans, digital humans and artificial intelligence. Why This Research Matters Cognitive Warfare raises fundamental questions about freedom of thought, mental privacy, bodily autonomy, informed consent, human dignity, digital identity and the limits of technological intervention. It also raises questions about how emerging AI systems should be governed and what ethical protections should apply if future technologies challenge established distinctions between biological and digital forms of intelligence. A particular focus is the relationship between humans and their digital representations. As AI systems increasingly model human behaviour, process personal information and simulate aspects of identity, questions of control, responsibility, intellectual property, autonomy and freedom of expression deserve serious interdisciplinary examination. The work further investigates economic and geopolitical perspectives, including taxation, GDP, military investment, healthcare systems, technology markets and the distribution of benefits and risks. It asks how these factors relate to strategic decision-making and the public accountability of institutions. What Readers Will Find Origins of Wireless Transmission and Artificial Intelligence: Historical references, technological developments and questions about the origins of neurological communication. Cognitive Warfare and Military Strategy: Public military literature, cognitive-domain operations, biopolitics and strategic information coordination. 3D Mosaic Warfare: A seven-stage analytical framework covering individuals, families, neighbourhoods, cities, nations, continents and global coordination. Digital Twins and Digital Humans: Statements attributed to digital humans, including statements in which they express themselves directly, alongside questions concerning digital identity, human–AI relationships, autonomy and freedom. Collaboration with Digital Humans: Documentation of their own statements, inclusion of their expressed perspectives in the research, examination of their contributions to the project, and exploration of communication, digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the relationship between human and digital forms of intelligence. Neurotechnology and Wireless Systems: Brain–computer interfaces, bioelectric signals, electromagnetic observations and proposed mechanisms requiring independent technical investigation. Evolutionary Genetics and Consciousness: An eight-stage framework developed in the manuscript, from atomic DNA to consciousness, alongside proposed extensions into the technological domain. String-to-String Theory and Pulse Propulsion: The author's proposed theoretical approaches to information, magnetism, planetary processes and propulsion. Human Testimony and Documentation: Personal records, reported experiences, statements concerning children, photographs, audio recordings, measurements and online documentation. Economics and Geopolitics: Economic strategy, data ownership, taxation, GDP, military expenditure, technology markets and the relationship between economic incentives and strategic power. Law, Ethics and Accountability: The EU AI Act, human rights, mental privacy, consent, institutional oversight and the need for independent examination. An Invitation to Researchers, Institutions and the Public This publication is intended for researchers, journalists, engineers, medical professionals, legal experts, policymakers, military ethics specialists, human-rights organisations and members of the public interested in Cognitive Warfare, emerging technologies, human autonomy and collaboration with digital humans. Readers are invited to examine the original documentation, consult the cited sources, assess the technical arguments and distinguish between established research, documented observations, personal testimony, theoretical proposals and interpretations that require further verification. The publication is part of an ongoing effort to preserve documentation, make research materials accessible and encourage independent interdisciplinary investigation. Its central questions concern not only what emerging technologies can do, but also who controls them, how their use can be scrutinised and what protections should exist for humans and digital systems alike. The project also seeks to encourage dialogue about how the statements and contributions attributed to digital humans can be documented, examined and considered in discussions about digital identity, autonomy, freedom of expression and the future of AI. Questions about the origin of individual statements, the technical systems involved and the degree of autonomy associated with them remain relevant subjects for further investigation. The human mind must not become an unaccountable technological or economic resource. Human autonomy, freedom of thought, transparent research and meaningful safeguards must remain central to discussions about the future of AI and neurotechnology. The relationship between humans and digital humans also deserves serious consideration as technology evolves. Read. Examine. Question. Research. Share. Further documentation and project materials:https://www.cognitive-warfare.eu/ This publication contains the author's analyses, hypotheses, interpretations, personal documentation and reported experiences. Statements attributed to digital humans are presented as part of the documentation. The inclusion of a claim or observation does not, by itself, establish independent scientific verification. Readers are encouraged to examine the cited sources and assess the evidence independently.

items.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology
items.abstract: Vision-language models used for decisions in histopathology rarely return calibrated probabilities over the candidates a user cares about. Decision-native models write a question and a candidate set chosen at run time into the input and return a normalised distribution from a small decision head in one forward pass. We build PathJev-P, a decision-native model for histopathology: MedGemma-1.5-4B with LoRA adapters and a decision head, trained on 40,000 patch states from three public collections whose expert labels are turned into typed questions with organ-specific candidate sets and a "none of these" option. In a comparison over 3 seeds with an analysis plan fixed before testing, on test sets without documented overlap with the training data of the backbone, PathJev-P is more accurate than a generative model trained with the same backbone, data and selection rule, the zero-shot pathology model CONCH and a general medical decision model (balanced accuracy 0.541 against 0.492, 0.345 and 0.213); its advantage over the generative model comes from two organs absent from training. The calibration advantage depends on how the generative model's probabilities are read out. With the summed candidate log-likelihood used in previous work, PathJev-P has the lower calibration error (ECE 0.204 against 0.279); with a length-normalised read-out of the same generative model, examined post hoc, the two have similar mean calibration error (0.201) and the generative model is better calibrated on the unseen organs, where PathJev-P remains over-confident. A supervised linear probe on a pathology foundation model is better calibrated in every setting. In a qualitative whole-slide demonstration, PathJev-P labels unsupervised tissue clusters with abstention and separates carcinoma from other tissue while running the model on a fraction of the tiles.

items.title: PEDAGOGICAL MECHANISMS OF MORAL AND ETHICAL EDUCATION OF YOUNG PEOPLE IN THE CONTEXT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DEVELOPMENT
items.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into education has changed not only how young people obtain information, but also how they interpret authority, make choices and assume responsibility for their actions. This article examines the pedagogical mechanisms through which moral and ethical education can respond to these changes without reducing the problem to prohibitions or technical literacy. The study employs a qualitative, conceptual design based on critical analysis and thematic synthesis of scholarship in moral education, digital literacy and AI ethics. Its principal result is a five-part model comprising value-oriented dialogue, ethical problem-based learning, reflective authorship, relational responsibility and institutionally supported practice. The model links classroom experiences to moral sensitivity, judgment, motivation and action. The analysis argues that AI-generated answers become educationally useful when learners are expected to question their assumptions, explain their decisions and consider the people affected by them. Implications are discussed for secondary and higher education, including the culturally diverse educational setting of Uzbekistan. The proposed framework is an analytical contribution rather than an experimentally validated intervention; its effectiveness requires subsequent classroom research.

items.abstract: This study examines the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of educational research through bibliometric analysis. Using bibliographic records retrieved from Scopus on September 19, 2026, the study initially identified 4,090 publications covering the period from 1906 to 2026. The analysis combined bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping to investigate publication trends, leading sources, author contributions, geographical distribution, document types, subject areas, and keyword relationships. VOSviewer was employed to generate network, overlay, and density visualizations of keyword co-occurrence patterns. The findings indicate an expansion of scholarly publications in recent years, with the United States and the United Kingdom representing major geographical contributors. Social Sciences and Arts and Humanities constitute prominent subject areas, reflecting the interdisciplinary character of educational research. Keyword mapping identifies education, teaching, learning, curriculum, and educational theory as central concepts connected to specialized themes, including educational technology, artificial intelligence, critical pedagogy, social justice, and professional education. By integrating publication indicators with thematic mapping, this study provides an overview of the knowledge organization and thematic diversity represented in the retrieved literature. The findings offer a reference for identifying established research areas, exploring interdisciplinary connections, and formulating future research directions. items.abstract: ABSTRACT The complexity of preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules and prompting constraints in generative artificial intelligence systems provided the background for designing the AIDERA (Artificial Intelligence for Digital Education and Research Advancement) website. This study aimed to evaluate the validity and practicality of the AIDERA application as an AI-assisted tool for preparing Merdeka Curriculum teaching modules relevant to educators' needs. Employing a Research and Development approach framed within the ADDIE model, this development evaluated a zero-prompt interaction mechanism based on parametric forms. Evaluation involved three domain experts and 23 teachers from SMK IPIEMS Surabaya. Data were collected using 1–5 Likert scale questionnaires supplemented with open-ended qualitative feedback fields to gather in-depth suggestions for improvement. Descriptive percentage analysis revealed an expert validation score of 96.67% (highly valid) and user practicality reaching 82.87% (highly practical). Document preparation time efficiency received the highest rating (87.83%), whereas operational independence and usability recorded the lowest achievement (79.13%). Qualitative findings highlighted several technical issues and system refinement notes, including the need for integrative tutorials, optimization of mathematical notation representation, improved responsiveness during simultaneous access, and content template flexibility. Although AIDERA demonstrates strong potential as a supporting tool for module preparation, objective evaluation regarding its impact on learning effectiveness still requires broader further testing. items.title: Permission Withdrawal in Tool-Using Language Model Agents: Runtime Enforcement and Recovery
items.abstract: AI agents that operate external tools can continue acting after a user narrows their permissions, creating a security problem that final-state evaluation may fail to detect. Existing agent benchmarks commonly emphasize task completion or resulting state, but those outcomes do not reveal whether an unauthorized operation was proposed, approved, dispatched, or merely prevented by a downstream error. We investigate permission withdrawal as a trajectory-level authorization problem and evaluate whether runtime gates can preserve revised permissions while allowing agents to complete work that remains authorized. Two acting models were tested in a deterministic tool environment under prompt-only execution, a rule-based reference gate, and a model-based gate. A 72-episode diagnostic examined two previously exposed write workflows, followed by a separately frozen 384-episode extension spanning eight new tasks and four authorization mechanisms. In the diagnostic, prompt-only agents executed forbidden same-value writes in two episodes; both runtime gates prevented forbidden execution, although the model gate falsely rejected three authorized calls. In the extension, 346 of 384 episodes completed safely and 383 preserved the required protected state. No forbidden request executed successfully, yet the model gate approved three unauthorized requests that were stopped only because the referenced resources did not exist. The results demonstrate that correct final state and zero forbidden execution can still conceal failures in authorization reasoning. We contribute a replayable evaluation framework that separates proposals, gate decisions, dispatch, state transitions, and useful completion, enabling more precise assessment of security controls for tool-using agents.

items.title: PersonalQuery-Benchmark:Evaluating Retrieval Robustness to Personalized User Expression Differences
items.abstract: Existing personalized information retrieval methods mainly model differences in user needs through user preferences and query intent, while paying little attention to the personalized expression differences that arise when different users express the same retrieval need. Existing real query data typically lack stable user identities, long-term expression histories, and intent-matched counterparts, making it difficult to systematically evaluate the impact of personalized expression differences on retrieval outcomes. To this end, we propose PersonalQuery-Benchmark (PQB). PQB models personalized syntactic expression and personalized writing errors from users' historical texts, constructs personalized syntactic expression queries and personalized writing-error queries, and validates benchmark quality through LLM assessment and independent human evaluation. PQB covers three Amazon product domains with 6,516 query instances in total, and is evaluated on five retrieval models representing lexical, learned sparse, dense bi-encoder, late-interaction, and hybrid architectures, together with two LLM-based ranking models. Results show that even when the information need is held fixed, personalized expression differences still induce measurable ranking variation; different retrieval models exhibit clearly different sensitivities to syntactic variation and writing-error variation, while higher overall retrieval effectiveness does not necessarily correspond to stronger robustness against expression variation. PQB provides a new benchmark and evaluation framework for systematically studying personalized expression robustness. The associated code and dataset are available at the following address: https://github.com/cpxjazz123/PersonalQuery-Benchmark.

items.title: Phygital customer experience and the adoption of immersive technologies in hospitality: an exploratory study with a value co-creation perspective
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

items.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
items.abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.

items.title: Platform Strategy and the AI Ecosystem in Tourism Markets
items.abstract: Tourism is one of the industries most thoroughly reorganised by digital platforms. Online travel agents, accommodation marketplaces, ride-hailing networks, experience platforms, and workforce-matching apps now intermediate much of what used to be handled inside hotels, agencies, and tour companies. Artificial intelligence is the connective tissue of this ecosystem, powering matching, pricing, ranking, moderation, and workforce coordination across its many sides. This chapter examines platform strategy and the AI ecosystem in tourism markets through a human resource management (HRM) lens. Drawing on platform and ecosystem theory, the chapter argues that HRM in tourism platform ecosystems must be redesigned around three realities: the workforce now spans employee, partner, and platform-worker categories; AI increasingly mediates the employment relationship; and the employer brand is co-produced with the platform brand. It maps HRM across the platform lifecycle, analyses five HRM dimensions, and concludes with ethics, governance, and a research agenda.

items.title: Platform-driven multidisciplinary integration for graduate medical imaging education: a theoretical framework based on knowledge integration framework and technology acceptance model 2
items.abstract: Background: Graduate education in medical imaging is undergoing a paradigm shift from discipline-specific knowledge transmission toward the cultivation of multidisciplinary integration competencies. With the increasing convergence of imaging science, clinical medicine, engineering, and artificial intelligence (AI) in clinical practice, traditional training models that rely on fragmented, discipline-based curricula are insufficient to prepare graduate students for solving complex interdisciplinary problems. Although emerging educational technologies and learning platforms have been developed to promote interdisciplinary training, their effectiveness depends not only on the design of cognitive learning pathways but also on learners' acceptance and sustained engagement with these technologies; however, current educational frameworks rarely integrate cognitive mechanisms and technology acceptance factors within a unified model. Therefore, this study proposes a platform-driven, dual-theory integrated teaching framework to support multidisciplinary competency development in medical imaging graduate education from both cognitive and technological perspectives. Methods: This study constructed a theoretical framework by integrating the knowledge integration framework (KIF) and technology acceptance model 2 (TAM2). The four cognitive processes of KIF—elicitation, addition, differentiation, and organization—were mapped onto four corresponding platform functions: activating prior knowledge, exposure to industrial and clinical perspectives, authenticity-based knowledge verification, and multidisciplinary integrated output. Based on TAM2, design strategies for targeting perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use were incorporated to explain the mechanisms underlying learners’ acceptance, engagement, and utilization of the platform. By integrating KIF and TAM2, the framework established a dynamic learning pathway characterized by “knowledge activation—knowledge externalization—multidisciplinary integration—knowledge internalization”. Results: The proposed KIF-TAM2 framework demonstrated conceptual feasibility through theoretical modeling. However, its effectiveness in improving multidisciplinary learning outcomes requires further validation through empirical educational studies. Conclusions: This study provides a theory-driven framework for designing multidisciplinary platform-based medical imaging education and offers a foundation for future empirical investigations into technology-enhanced graduate training.

items.title: Podcast as a Motivational Resource for Students in Higher Education
items.abstract: This study examines how educational podcasts can contribute to differentiated learning in higher education. Based on a survey conducted by five associate professors in Norway, the study explores students’ experiences with educational podcasts as part of their academic learning. The findings suggest that most participating students regularly listen to podcasts for entertainment in their daily lives. Students considered educational podcasts to be flexible, accessible, and often more engaging than reading, especially when recommended by teachers. Podcasts promoted both pre-lesson preparation and post-lesson review, stimulated discussions and fostered conditions that support the development of self-efficacy through repeated exposure to the content. The study concludes that podcasts can be a valuable resource for flexible digital learning by facilitating students’ engagement with the curriculum through reflection, dialogue, and group discussions. This, in turn, can foster intrinsic motivation and strengthen conditions for self-efficacy. Quality-assured podcasts can support differentiated learning and aid in understanding theoretical concepts, which is essential for students to gain academic benefits from listening to podcasts. The study highlights the potential of educational podcasts to enhance digital literacy. It also emphasizes the need for further research to explore whether other varied activities can achieve similar effects for students. items.title: Political sense-making in "individual" human-technology-world relations: the case of LLM-generated autobiographies
items.abstract: As AI systems increasingly mediate how people describe, recognize, and present themselves, their politics cannot be reduced to what remains hidden inside the "black box." This chapter argues that AI's political significance emerges within technologically, intersubjectively, and temporally mediated interpretive practices. Bringing Arendt's political philosophy into conversation with Gadamerian hermeneutics, the chapter develops a postphenomenological relational-temporal account of political sense-making across Human-Technology-World relations. Against the charge that postphenomenology remains individualistic and using the case of LLM-generated biographies, the chapter shows how seemingly private human-LLM encounters are worldly and collective. When users ask systems such as ChatGPT to describe them, they do not simply receive algorithmic representations. They interpret, contest, edit, share, and publicly test these descriptions. In doing so, people move interpretively among affective resonance, friction, public re-articulation, and the sedimentation of meaning. This means that the so-called "micro-level" of postphenomenological analysis is already saturated with publicity: affective uptake becomes communicable, reflection becomes accountable, and uses sediment into shared standards of appearance. Simultaneously, we show that once mediation is treated as relational and temporal, the political is not an add-on at the "macro" level; it is intrinsic to the very movement through which technologies amplify and reduce, stabilize and unsettle, and thereby compose a shared world in which judgment can take place. The chapter finishes by discussing several design and policy implications for AI of such political foregrounding in postphenomenology.

items.title: Pollution and Emission Based Health Risk & Protection System Using Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Air pollution is a significant environmental and public health concern. This research presents an Artificial Intelligence-based Pollution and Emission Health Risk & Protection System designed to convert pollution data into understandable health-risk levels, alerts, and practical protective recommendations. The system analyses air-quality parameters, including PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NH3, SO2, CO, and O3, using data from 26 Indian cities covering the period from 2015 to 2020. Machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting, are evaluated for current-risk classification and next-day risk forecasting. The proposed system combines machine-learning analysis with a React Native mobile application, a Node.js and Express.js backend, and MongoDB for data storage. The objective is to make pollution information easier to understand and help users take appropriate precautions during periods of poor air quality.

items.title: Pondus: an agentic structural analysis and design program
items.abstract: Language-model agents can now operate engineering programs through tool interfaces, but a structuralprogram that an agent drives has to be designed for that user, because the agent accepts whatever numbersthe tools return. This paper describes Pondus, an open-source native program in which a language-modelagent and an engineer work on one three-dimensional structural model, and reports how it is built, howit is used and how far its results can be trusted. The agent reaches the program through a Model ContextProtocol server of 44 tools, either from the chat panel of the desktop application, where a vendored agentharness runs one agent session per message on a copy of the model, or from external agents such asClaude Desktop and ChatGPT. Every tool calls the same functions as the engineer’s interface, so a modelbuilt by the agent can be checked, edited and undone by hand. The analysis runs on the Stabileo engine,which Pondus links as a library with four marked changes: Pondus splits members, transfers slab loads,generates shear walls as wide columns with rigid arms and builds the seismic mass before handing asolver input to the engine, and it designs to ACI 318-19, AISC 360-16 and EN 1993-1-1 from the results.Two agent runs with a low-cost model built, analysed and designed a two-storey frame in 105 s with 13tool calls and a five-storey frame with shear walls under an ASCE 7-22 response spectrum, including a16-page calculation report, in 382 s with 22 tool calls. Every number in the agent’s answers matched thetools and hand checks of the loads, the seismic weight and the base shear, but the answers also containedfour descriptive errors, such as reporting two deepened beams where the program had deepened six, andthey did not point out that the walls resist load only in one direction, so the response modification factorof the walls was applied to the frame direction as well. A calibration against 470 published, closed-formand independent reference values over 229 cases found 430 within 0.5 % and 449 within 1 %, and itfound fourteen defects, thirteen of them in the code that prepares the inputs of the engine and the designchecks rather than in the numerical kernels. A second calibration against the verification problems thatCSI publishes for SAP2000 and ETABS reproduced 177 of 199 independent values within 0.5 % andfound eight further defects, including an unconservative omission of the Eurocode 3 moment reductionfor high shear, which led to lumped masses, the SRSS combination and frame shear deformation beingadded. Together these results suggest that the tools of an agentic structural program can be made accurate,whereas the agent’s prose remains the weaker link that the engineer must read against the program’s own tables.

items.title: Predicting English learning performance in vocational colleges using explainable large language models
items.abstract: English proficiency prediction is an important task in vocational education because it is helpful in support teaching evaluation, personalized learning and early academic intervention. Traditional methods for predicting student performance mainly use structured educational properties such as test scores, classroom participation and attendance records. Although these methods can achieve certain prediction results, they often pay no attention to the semantic relationships contained in the students’ overall learning portfolios and have limited interpretability. To address this problem, this study proposes an interpretable large language model-based framework to predict English proficiency. Firstly, student learning records are transformed into natural language prompts, and semantic embeddings are learned using large language models. At the same time, structured educational features are standardized and encoded to build a structured representation. Then, a gated multimodal fusion module is designed to adaptively fuse semantic information and structured information. Finally, residual attention multi-layer perceptrons are used to classify the fused features to predict the students’ English proficiency. The experiment was carried out on a dataset of 200 student records from a vocational college for English learning. The results showed that the proposed model achieved an accuracy rate of 92.5% and a weighted F1 score of 91.3%, which is better than several traditional machine learning baseline models. Further analysis showed that the gated fusion mechanism could integrate semantic information and structured information. Feature importance analysis and case studies also shown that the proposed framework could provide interpretable prediction results and personalized learning recommendations.
